incidents.name: Degraded availability for GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages and Webhooks

incident_updates.body:
On October 19, 2026, between 15:24 and 16:52 UTC, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, and webhooks generated by Actions were degraded. Live updates on GitHub.com and code search were also degraded for part of this time. No data was lost.

Impact

- Workflow status updates, logs, and checks were delayed.
- 5.13% of jobs on GitHub-hosted runners were delayed in starting, and 0.02% of workflow runs failed.
- During the first 30 minutes, 8.47% of requests to the Actions jobs REST API returned errors.

Pages deployments and webhooks generated by Actions runs were delayed.

An internal Actions service that stores logs and run status lost connections to some of its cache servers in one cloud region and immediately retried them from every server at once. The resulting surge of new connections overloaded a shared network link between our data center and that region, which also disrupted other services that use the same link. We mitigated the incident by moving the Actions service off the affected cache servers and reducing connections from other services on the link. We then processed the delayed Actions work. We are continuing to investigate the cause of the initial connection timeouts.

We were already in the process of rolling out a limit on how quickly this service can open new connections, but it was still in shadow mode (logging only, not enforcing) at the time of the incident. We have since fully enforced it and capped the service's concurrent connection attempts. We are extending these limits to other Actions services, adding backoff to retries, limiting how much shared network capacity a single service can use, and improving alerting so we can find the source of connection surges faster.
Actions, Pages and Webhooks are operating normally.

We’re seeing recovery following mitigation and are continuing to monitor.

Customers may still experience delays in GitHub Actions workflow status updates, GitHub Pages deployments, and check and workflow webhook events generated by Actions runs.

We’re are currently investigating degraded availability affecting GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages and Webhooks.

Customers may experience delays in workflow processing, site builds and webhook delivery.
Webhooks is experiencing degraded performance. We are continuing to investigate.
We are investigating reports of degraded performance for Actions and Pages

incidents.name: Incident with Actions, Pull Requests and Issues

incident_updates.body:
On October 12th 2026 11:51 UTC GitHub experienced elevated 500 responses across several application pages. This caused failures on Issues and Pull Requests as well as Projects and Actions. Customers also experienced delayed notifications in their web inbox and via email.

The immediate impact to Issues, Pull Requests, Projects, and Actions was mitigated by 12:41 UTC on October 12th. Notifications deliveries to the web inbox and via email were recovering at 15:27 UTC and fully mitigated by 20:16 UTC.

The incident was triggered through a latent condition in our notifications delivery pipeline that put a high volume of an expensive query on our sharded database replicas. This reduced available database capacity to serve requests for Issues, Pull Requests, Projects, and Actions.

We have fixed the notifications pipeline’s code path that issued the expensive query. We are also improving resilience of the database layer to reduce the likelihood and impact of similar incidents.
